summary: The article surveys strategies for managing chronic conditions such as heart disease, diabetes, arthritis and dementia as populations age. It covers integrated care models, telemedicine, prevention programs, patient education, government and non-profit grants, and interdisciplinary training of healthcare professionals. It concludes that coordinated effort and ongoing research are needed to help seniors stay healthy and independent.
one_line: Overview of 2023 initiatives for managing chronic diseases in older adults, from integrated care and telehealth to prevention, education, grants and training.
key_facts: The WHO projects the share of the world's population over 60 will double from 12% to 22% between 2015 and 2050.
A CDC report released on September 15, 2023 found about 80% of older adults have at least one chronic health condition and 77% have at least two.
The WHO introduced the Integrated Care for Older People (ICOPE) approach in October 2023, emphasizing person-centered, integrated clinical care for the elderly.
Dr. Emily Stevenson says ICOPE looks at each patient holistically, with plans that can include medication management, physical therapy, dietary advice and mental health support.

A study published November 3, 2023 by the Journal of Geriatric Medicine found telehealth consultations improved chronic disease management in the elderly, with fewer hospital readmissions and better patient satisfaction.
Dr. Robert Harris, a telehealth pioneer, called the adoption of telemedicine in geriatrics necessary and overwhelmingly positive.
On September 18, 2023, the National Institute on Aging launched the 'Fit for Your Age' program to educate seniors on regular exercise and a balanced diet.
The Chronic Disease SelfManagement Program (CDSMP), which began in late 2023, offers courses to help patients cope with pain, fatigue and the psychological impact of chronic disease.
On September 1, 2023, the American Aging Association introduced a grant program to fund local communities developing interventions for chronic diseases among seniors.
John Franklin, head of the government-funded program, says the aim is a sustainable approach that helps seniors manage chronic conditions and maintain independence.
Melissa Chang, a nurse educator, leads a collaborative program started October 12, 2023 among nurses, physicians, pharmacists and social workers.
Clinical trials are underway exploring new medications, therapies and lifestyle interventions for chronic conditions in seniors.
